newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar ends firmer, seen edging higher.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar ends firmer, seen edging higher.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer on Tuesday and looked set to test higher before its downtrend resumed, dealers said.
"A local bank here seems to have buying interest, and has done for the last two or three hours."
The kiwi closed at US$0.6465/72 and at 64.67 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6424/31 and 64.32 at the open.
The kiwi had been hammered over three-quarters of a cent during the overnight session, reaching a low of 0.6405 before bouncing slightly in its local market this morning.

"The downtrend looked as though it had been reasserted last night. It broke the previous week's low at 0.6453, we then took out the '95 low at 0.6428/30. We should really have called for lower levels," the dealer said.

"At one stage today we had a bounce to 0.6445 and then it became offered again. But on the second time through 0.6450 I think it squeezed shorts on the day and caused a buy order from one of the local banks, and he's still covering that.
"So the market got whipped a little bit in terms of the view today," he said.
"I think the traders were a little bit caught. They were possibly expecting a lower level today which we never saw."
Exporters had been buyers over the course of the session.
Dealers saw the kiwi edging higher overnight, possibly as high as 65 U.S. cents, before the downside was attacked again.
